comment: Wiggins is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat due to a left knee contusion.
detail: Wiggins is dealing with a bruised knee, so he might skip the first game in Atlanta's upcoming back-to-back set. If he's not able to give it a go, Corey Kispert would have a chance for some meaningful run in the rotation.

comment: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
detail: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).

comment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

comment: Carter has been diagnosed with mononucleosis and is without a timetable for a return, Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reports.
detail: Carter missed Boston's final three preseason games with the illness and is now expected to miss time to begin the regular season. He can be considered week-to-week until Boston provides an update on his progress. The 2024 first-rounder signed a two-way pact with the Celtics on Saturday and will provide backcourt depth for the club.

comment: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
detail: Bilodeau will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right shoulder sprain. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

comment: Head coach Charles Lee said Monday that White (calf) remains without a timeline for a return, though Lee added that he'll have a better idea of where things stand following the Hornets' two-game road trip, Rod Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
detail: White's next opportunity to play will come Saturday at home against the Sixers in the second leg of a back-to-back set. However, he should be considered highly questionable for that contest until the Hornets offer an update on his status. Dennis Schroder and Christian Anderson will likely continue seeing increased burn until White returns.

comment: Knueppel (hamstring) is without a timetable for a return, Rod Boone of The Charlotte Observer reports.
detail: Knueppel has yet to take the floor this season while on the mend from a left hamstring strain, and at this point in time, the team isn't ready to commit to a return date. Coach Charles Lee stated before Monday's game against Washington that he could have more clarity on the plan for Knueppel following the two-game road trip, which wraps up Friday in Washington.

comment: Williams (hamstring) will be re-evaluated following Charlotte's upcoming two-game road trip, Rod Boone reports.
detail: Williams' earliest possible return date now looks to be Saturday at home against the 76ers. Royce O'Neale should continue to play meaning minutes off the bench for the Hornets in the interim.

comment: Boswell (knee) is out for Wednesday's season opener against the Nets.
detail: Boswell continues to rehab after right knee surgery. The hope in early October was that he would be cleared for basketball activities prior to the start of the G League season, which begins in early November.

comment: Williams (groin) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
detail: Williams is in danger of missing his third straight game Wednesday. However, even when healthy, he was not in the rotation.

comment: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
detail: The rookie big man is battling an ankle sprain. Zach Collins could pick up a few extra minutes off the bench if Awaka is out Wednesday.

comment: Claxton (hamstring) participated in individual drills Monday morning and hopes to join the team for practice next week, Joe Cowley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
detail: The Bulls reported one week ago that the big man would be re-evaluated in two weeks, so he appears to be right on track with his recovery from a hamstring injury. He'll presumably need to take part in 5-on-5 drills before getting the green light to return to game action.

comment: Biberovic is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Biberovic isn't expected to play Wednesday due to right heel bursitis, though the doubtful tag represents a step in the right direction. However, his potential absence wouldn't affect the rotation.

comment: Aldama (knee) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: While Aldama is unlikely to play Wednesday, he appears to be making progress after being sent down to Dallas' G League affiliate on a rehab assignment. Aldama is not expected to have a significant role in the Mavs' rotation this season.

comment: De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: De Larrea sustained a right knee sprain in Monday's win over the Heat and will be held out of Wednesday's contest. His next chance to play will come Friday against Houston. With the rookie guard sidelined, Marcus Sasser could see a slight bump in minutes.

comment: Martin (thumb) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Martin has a chance to make his season debut Wednesday. Look for the Mavericks to update his status closer to tipoff.

comment: Marshall (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Marshall is looking to return from an illness Wednesday. Zaccharie Risacher would likely play a larger role off the bench if Marshall remains sidelined.

comment: Irving (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Irving could receive a maintenance day Wednesday. If the star guard is sidelined, Marcus Sasser would likely handle an expanded role at point guard while Cooper Flagg takes on more usage.

comment: Lively (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Pacers.
detail: Lively underwent right foot surgery last December and remains without a clear timetable to return. The big man can be considered week-to-week until the Mavericks offer an update on his status. In the meantime, Moussa Cisse and Morez Johnson are candidates for increased minutes.

comment: Jones (hamstring) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against New Orleans.
detail: Jones is reportedly progressing in his recovery, though there's still no firm timetable for his return to game action. He can be considered week-to-week until the Nuggets provide an update on his status.

comment: Johnson (ankle) is doubtful to face the Pelicans on Wednesday.
detail: Johnson is on track to miss his third straight game Wednesday. Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile will continue to help pick up the slack in Johnson's absence.

comment: Diallo is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans due to personal reasons.
detail: Diallo appears to have moved past a wrist injury but is now attending to a personal matter. His next chance to rejoin the Nuggets comes Friday in Phoenix.

comment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

comment: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Knicks.
detail: Joe will miss the front end of this back-to-back set due to a right hip contusion. With the 27-year-old wing sidelined, Javonte Green, Kevin Huerter and Ronald Holland are all candidates to see a bump in minutes off the bench.

comment: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Duren suffered the hamstring injury in Friday's win over Miami and is set to miss an extended period. Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

comment: Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
detail: The rookie standout is in danger of missing his first game of the season Wednesday with foot soreness. With the Warriors already short on forward options, Georges Niang could be thrust into a starting role if Lendeborg cannot play.

comment: Porzingis is contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: Charania also notes Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Porzingis, who is already considered out indefinitely to begin the 2026-27 season. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect the big man to get back on the floor anytime soon, whether it be for the Warriors or perhaps another team, and it sounds like stepping away from the game is on the table for Porzingis at this point.

comment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

comment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

comment: Smart (forearm) is questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Bucks.
detail: Smart is at risk of missing a third straight game with a forearm strain. Reed Sheppard and Tari Eason would remain locked into big roles off the bench if Smart is unable to suit up.

comment: Sengun (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
detail: Sengun is dealing with lower-back soreness and will miss his first game of the season, with his next chance to play coming Friday at Dallas. Tari Eason and Clint Capela are both candidates to see increased playing time in Sengun's stead.

comment: Head coach Ime Udoka said Monday that Adams could be out "a week or two" due to his right soleus strain, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
detail: The veteran big man can be considered week-to-week until the Rockets offer another update on his status. In the meantime, Clint Capela will likely see increased playing time behind Alperen Sengun.

comment: Nembhard (neck) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
detail: Nembhard is still dealing with soreness in his neck and could miss a second straight game. The 26-year-old guard's absence would open up additional minutes for guys like Quenton Jackson, Braden Smith and Jarace Walker, especially if Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) is downgraded from questionable to out.

comment: Haliburton is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the 76ers due to left hamstring tightness.
detail: The left hamstring issue is a new concern for Haliburton, who has yet to miss a game this season. If the star floor general joins T.J. McConnell (hamstring) on the inactive list, Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith would likely see increased burn.

comment: Toppin is probable to play Wednesday against the 76ers due to a left hand sprain.
detail: Toppin is dealing with a sprained shooting hand, but it's not expected to keep him out of Wednesday's game. Through the first four games of the season, Toppin is averaging 15.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 triples per contest on 55/40/74 shooting splits.

comment: Nesmith (hamstring) is probable for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
detail: Nesmith has been slowly ramping up after missing some of the preseason and Indiana's first regular-season game with a hamstring injury, so it'll be interesting to see if his minutes are bumped up Wednesday. Through the first three games of the year, Nesmith is averaging 11.7 points and 2.0 triples in 20 minutes per contest.

comment: McConnell (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
detail: The veteran point guard continues to battle a hamstring strain. His next chance to make his season debut comes Friday in Miami.

comment: Zubac (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
detail: Zubac isn't ready to return from an ankle sprain, but the veteran big man remains day-to-day. Jay Huff figures to continue starting for the Pacers in the meantime, with Obi Toppin (hand) also helping plug up the hole at center.

comment: Sheppard is scheduled for surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee Wednesday, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports.
detail: Sheppard was diagnosed with a torn left meniscus Friday, and the team has since determined that he'll require surgery. A timetable for the guard's return should start to come into focus after the procedure.

comment: Furphy was diagnosed with a torn right ACL on Monday and will miss the remainder of the season, Michael Scotto of USA Today reports.
detail: Furphy started in 21 of 35 regular-season appearances for the Pacers, posting averages of 5.1 points, 4.4 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.7 three-pointers in 18.4 minutes per contest. While no timetable has been announced, Furphy's absence could extend through the beginning of the 2026-27 season. With this news, the Pacers will likely lean more on Ben Sheppard, Kam Jones and Quenton Jackson moving forward.

comment: Hachimura (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.
detail: Hachimura didn't practice Tuesday and will be held out of Wednesday's contest due to left quad soreness. His next opportunity to play will come Friday at Minnesota. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

comment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

comment: Strus has been diagnosed with a partially torn plantar fascia in his right foot and he will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Plantar fascia injuries can be tricky to recover from, with the only remedy typically being prolonged rest, so don't be surprised if Strus' absence extends well beyond this initial four-week window. With Strus now set to miss at least the first few weeks of the season, and Bradley Beal (knee) uncertain for opening night, Keaton Wagler could be thrust into the first unit sooner than expected.

comment: Niederhauser (foot) won't be ready for the start of the season, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
detail: Niederhauser is progressing from March surgery but won't be able to suit up to begin the year. The Clippers are likely to take a cautious approach with the 2025 first-rounder. Isaiah Jackson should occupy the backup center spot behind Brook Lopez early in the campaign.

comment: Ingram won't be ready for the start of the season due to a partially torn Achilles, per Joey Linn of SI.com.
detail: The Clippers learned about the injury this summer, though it's unclear exactly how far along Ingram is in his recovery. The star forward's timeline for a return is unclear, clouding his fantasy outlook in the meantime. Darius Garland should take on all the usage he can handle in Ingram's stead, while Kris Dunn and Max Strus could have additional streaming appeal early in the year.

comment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

comment: Thiero (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against Portland.
detail: Thiero continues to miss time due to swelling in his left knee. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Wednesday against the Clippers.

comment: Larsson is listed as probable for Wednesday's game at Atlanta due to a right ankle sprain.
detail: The ankle injury is a new concern for Larsson, though he's still expected to suit up for Wednesday's contest. The 25-year-old swingman is averaging 9.0 points, 3.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 30.8 minutes per game across four regular-season outings.

comment: Fontecchio is doubtful for Wednesday's game in Atlanta due to an illness, per Tim Reynolds of Associated Press.
detail: Fontecchio is unlikely to be available off the bench for the first time this season. His expected absence should have little impact on the Miami rotation.

comment: Edwards will undergo arthroscopic right knee surgery and is expected to miss up to two months, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: This is a tough blow after a torrid start to the season for Edwards, and it looks like we might not see him again until 2027. Ayo Dosunmu will likely be elevated to a starting role while Edwards is sidelined, while LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga will see a bump in usage. There will also be more minutes available for Terrence Shannon, Bones Hyland and Cody Williams.

comment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

comment: Poole (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Denver.
detail: Poole is under the weather but appears likely to suit up in the front end of this back-to-back set. Through three regular-season games, the veteran guard is averaging 7.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.7 minutes per contest.

comment: Missi has been diagnosed with a left knee bone bruise and he will miss an extended period of time, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Missi currently has no official timetable for his return, but he appears likely to miss significant time. Derik Queen could be elevated into a starting role while Missi is sidelined, so make sure he's not floating around on your waiver wire. Missi doesn't offer enough upside to warrant holding onto in re-draft fantasy leagues.

comment: Alvarado (ankle) is out for Tuesday's game against the Pistons.
detail: Alvarado is missing a second consecutive game with a sprained ankle. Tyler Kolek entered the New York rotation in Sunday's loss to the Magic and should continue to play a bench role while Alvarado is sidelined.

comment: Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
detail: Sorber is still without a firm timetable for a return to game action. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder provide an update on his progress.

comment: Holmgren (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks.
detail: Holmgren will miss a second consecutive contest due to right knee patellar tendinitis. With the big man and several other key pieces on the inactive list, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Brooks Barnhizer are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

comment: Topic (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game in Dallas.
detail: Topic has yet to play this season, and per standard Thunder protocol, Oklahoma City has not released any updates on where he is in his rehab. He should be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

comment: Mitchell (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
detail: Mitchell came away with an ankle sprain in the aftermath of Monday's win over the Suns. With Alex Caruso (ankle) already ruled out for Wednesday, Jared McCain would be streaming shallow fantasy leagues and Bennett Stirtz in deeper formats if Mitchell is sidelined.

comment: Caruso (ankle) won't play Wednesday in Dallas.
detail: Kenrich Williams and Bennett Stirtz should see a boost with Caruso on the inactive list for Wednesday's game. Caruso's next chance to play will come Saturday in Houston.

comment: Williams has been diagnosed with a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, which will require surgery, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Williams suffered the gruesome injury during Sunday's matchup against the Clippers and needed to be stretched off the court after a drive to the rim. He's expected to miss a significant chunk of the 2026-27 season while recovering, but the Thunder should have a better idea of a timeline for his return following surgery.

comment: Wallace has been diagnosed with a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will require surgery, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Although Wallace's return timetable has yet to be determined, Charania notes the guard is expected miss most of, if not all, of the rest of the season. It's been a brutal day for the Thunder, who also lost Jalen Williams (ankle) on Monday and will need Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain and Alex Caruso each to step up for the remainder of the year.

comment: The Thunder plan to waive Oweh (Achilles) on Friday.
detail: Oweh, a rookie second-round pick, was set to be a two-way player for Oklahoma City but suffered a ruptured right Achilles tendon in a preseason game, which will sideline him for the entire 2026-27 campaign. Following a long road to recovery, Oweh might have to settle for an Exhibit 10 deal next summer.

comment: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
detail: The oft-injured forward isn't ready to make his season debut. His next chance to do so arrives Friday in Toronto for a rematch with the Raptors.

comment: Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

comment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

comment: Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
detail: Penda suffered the hamstring tear in Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat. It's unknown how long the injury will keep the 21-year-old off the floor. However, since it's a different injury than the one he suffered in the same hamstring during training camp, the team may take a cautious approach regarding his return. Penda, the No. 32 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, averaged 3.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 12.8 minutes per outing in 59 regular-season games in 2025-26. While he's not expected to be a mainstay in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign, his absence could open up a few minutes for Tristan Da Silva.

comment: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
detail: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

comment: Fall (quadriceps) is out for Wednesday's game in Indiana.
detail: Fall was able to get through Tuesday's practice, but he'll remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game. He should continue to be viewed as week-to-week.

comment: Walker (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
detail: Walker will miss a second consecutive contest due to left knee soreness. According to Ky Carlin of USA Today, the 24-year-old forward didn't practice Tuesday but was able to go through individual on-court workouts. His next chance to play will come Friday against New York.

comment: Barlow will miss at least the next two weeks of action due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
detail: The back issue cost Barlow the entire preseason, and now he'll begin the regular season on the sidelines. The earliest we could see Barlow back on the court would be Nov. 2, but it wouldn't be shocking to see his absence extend beyond this loose, two-week window.

comment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

comment: Ighodaro (oblique) is out for Monday's matchup with the Thunder.
detail: Ighodaro remains sidelined with an oblique strain. Khaman Maluach should continue to start at center for the Suns and offer enhanced fantasy value as long as Ighodaro is out.

comment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

comment: Youngblood (ankle/two-way player) is out for Tuesday's game against the Lakers.
detail: It's unclear at this time whether Youngblood is still dealing with an ankle injury, or if this decision is simply because he's on a two-way contract. Either way, he's yet to make his 2026-27 debut and will need to wait at least until Thursday against the Grizzlies to do so.

comment: Henderson is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers due to left ankle soreness.
detail: Henderson is evidently dealing with some soreness following Friday's matchup in Sacramento. The Blazers should have a better idea of his availability after watching him go through shootaround and warmups ahead of Tuesday's tipoff.

comment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

comment: Cardwell (calf) will be re-evaluated in one week, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
detail: Cardwell is progressing well in his recovery from a calf strain. Precious Achiuwa should remain worth streaming in all fantasy leagues for the banged-up Kings in the meantime.

comment: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
detail: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

comment: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-to-14 days, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
detail: Murray has officially been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis, and he's set to miss at least the next 10 days. Precious Achiuwa has been starting in Murray's absence, and he should continue to see opportunities along with De'Andre Hunter and Daeqwon Plowden.

comment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

comment: Harris (calf) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Kings.
detail: Harris is still ramping up from a left calf strain and will miss a fourth consecutive contest to begin the regular season. His next opportunity to make his season debut will come Wednesday at Utah in the second leg of this back-to-back set. Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson will likely continue seeing increased playing time while Harris is sidelined.

comment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

comment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Magic, Cody Taylor of USA Today reports.
detail: Bittle remains without a timetable to return due to a right foot avulsion fracture. He can be considered week-to-week until the Raptors offer an update on his progress.

comment: Leonard (knee) is expected to miss multiple weeks due to swelling in his left knee, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: An MRI revealed no structural damage, but the Raptors will take a cautious approach with Leonard's recovery following interruptions to his offseason preparation. The veteran forward was a late scratch for Sunday's loss to Minnesota and now faces an extended absence just two games into the 2026-27 campaign. Allen Graves, who started in Leonard's place Sunday, figures to benefit from additional playing time, while RJ Barrett and Scottie Barnes could absorb more offensive responsibility.

comment: Hayes (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: With Jusuf Nurkic (toe) and Jaren Jackson (knee) both sidelined, the Jazz are thin at the center position. If Hayes is available versus the Spurs, he'll presumably start. If not, Kyle Filipowski would likely move into the starting lineup, with Mo Bamba getting more minutes off the bench.

comment: Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: Markkanen was forced out of Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies after spraining his wrist, but it looks like there's a chance he won't miss any additional game time. Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is also questionable for Wednesday's game, and if they both get cleared, Mo Bamba will lose some of his streaming appeal.

comment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

comment: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
detail: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

comment: Nurkic will miss at least the next four weeks due to a partial plantar plate tear of second toe in right foot, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
detail: Nurkic will begin the 2026-27 season on the sidelines, and given the tricky nature of foot injuries for big men, it wouldn't be shocking to see his absence extend beyond this initial four-week window. Jaren Jackson will likely spend more time at center while Nurkic is out, and there will be more minutes available for Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba.

comment: Champagnie (foot) is out for Wednesday's game versus Cleveland.
detail: Champagnie is sidelined by a right foot injury, which he picked up during Monday's loss in Charlotte. Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington make for intriguing streaming options in deeper fantasy leagues for Wednesday.

comment: Dybantsa (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game versus Cleveland.
detail: The rookie No. 1 overall pick has a chance to make his highly anticipated NBA debut Wednesday. His eventual return from an ankle sprain should push Bilal Coulibaly into a reserve role.

comment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Vukcevic (hip) will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
detail: Although the big man will remain a limited participant in training camp as he continues his rehab from a hip impingement, it sounds like his absence from game action will extend into the regular season. Deandre Ayton should have the backup center role all to himself until Vukcevic is cleared to retake the floor.

comment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

comment: Wiggins is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat due to a left knee contusion.
detail: Wiggins is dealing with a bruised knee, so he might skip the first game in Atlanta's upcoming back-to-back set. If he's not able to give it a go, Corey Kispert would have a chance for some meaningful run in the rotation.

comment: Williams (groin) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
detail: Williams is in danger of missing his third straight game Wednesday. However, even when healthy, he was not in the rotation.

comment: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
detail: The rookie big man is battling an ankle sprain. Zach Collins could pick up a few extra minutes off the bench if Awaka is out Wednesday.

comment: Marshall (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Marshall is looking to return from an illness Wednesday. Zaccharie Risacher would likely play a larger role off the bench if Marshall remains sidelined.

comment: Irving (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Irving could receive a maintenance day Wednesday. If the star guard is sidelined, Marcus Sasser would likely handle an expanded role at point guard while Cooper Flagg takes on more usage.

comment: Johnson (ankle) is doubtful to face the Pelicans on Wednesday.
detail: Johnson is on track to miss his third straight game Wednesday. Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile will continue to help pick up the slack in Johnson's absence.

comment: Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
detail: The rookie standout is in danger of missing his first game of the season Wednesday with foot soreness. With the Warriors already short on forward options, Georges Niang could be thrust into a starting role if Lendeborg cannot play.

comment: Smart (forearm) is questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Bucks.
detail: Smart is at risk of missing a third straight game with a forearm strain. Reed Sheppard and Tari Eason would remain locked into big roles off the bench if Smart is unable to suit up.

comment: Nembhard (neck) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
detail: Nembhard is still dealing with soreness in his neck and could miss a second straight game. The 26-year-old guard's absence would open up additional minutes for guys like Quenton Jackson, Braden Smith and Jarace Walker, especially if Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) is downgraded from questionable to out.

comment: Haliburton is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the 76ers due to left hamstring tightness.
detail: The left hamstring issue is a new concern for Haliburton, who has yet to miss a game this season. If the star floor general joins T.J. McConnell (hamstring) on the inactive list, Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith would likely see increased burn.

comment: Toppin is probable to play Wednesday against the 76ers due to a left hand sprain.
detail: Toppin is dealing with a sprained shooting hand, but it's not expected to keep him out of Wednesday's game. Through the first four games of the season, Toppin is averaging 15.8 points, 5.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.5 triples per contest on 55/40/74 shooting splits.

comment: Nesmith (hamstring) is probable for Wednesday's game against the 76ers.
detail: Nesmith has been slowly ramping up after missing some of the preseason and Indiana's first regular-season game with a hamstring injury, so it'll be interesting to see if his minutes are bumped up Wednesday. Through the first three games of the year, Nesmith is averaging 11.7 points and 2.0 triples in 20 minutes per contest.

comment: Larsson is listed as probable for Wednesday's game at Atlanta due to a right ankle sprain.
detail: The ankle injury is a new concern for Larsson, though he's still expected to suit up for Wednesday's contest. The 25-year-old swingman is averaging 9.0 points, 3.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 steals in 30.8 minutes per game across four regular-season outings.

comment: Fontecchio is doubtful for Wednesday's game in Atlanta due to an illness, per Tim Reynolds of Associated Press.
detail: Fontecchio is unlikely to be available off the bench for the first time this season. His expected absence should have little impact on the Miami rotation.

comment: Poole (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Denver.
detail: Poole is under the weather but appears likely to suit up in the front end of this back-to-back set. Through three regular-season games, the veteran guard is averaging 7.3 points, 4.0 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 18.7 minutes per contest.

comment: Mitchell (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
detail: Mitchell came away with an ankle sprain in the aftermath of Monday's win over the Suns. With Alex Caruso (ankle) already ruled out for Wednesday, Jared McCain would be streaming shallow fantasy leagues and Bennett Stirtz in deeper formats if Mitchell is sidelined.

comment: Ighodaro (oblique) is out for Monday's matchup with the Thunder.
detail: Ighodaro remains sidelined with an oblique strain. Khaman Maluach should continue to start at center for the Suns and offer enhanced fantasy value as long as Ighodaro is out.

comment: Henderson is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Lakers due to left ankle soreness.
detail: Henderson is evidently dealing with some soreness following Friday's matchup in Sacramento. The Blazers should have a better idea of his availability after watching him go through shootaround and warmups ahead of Tuesday's tipoff.

comment: Hayes (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: With Jusuf Nurkic (toe) and Jaren Jackson (knee) both sidelined, the Jazz are thin at the center position. If Hayes is available versus the Spurs, he'll presumably start. If not, Kyle Filipowski would likely move into the starting lineup, with Mo Bamba getting more minutes off the bench.

comment: Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: Markkanen was forced out of Monday's 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies after spraining his wrist, but it looks like there's a chance he won't miss any additional game time. Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is also questionable for Wednesday's game, and if they both get cleared, Mo Bamba will lose some of his streaming appeal.

comment: Carr was assigned to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Monday, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
detail: Carr is presumably getting some work in with LA's G League affiliate as he continues to battle his way back from an oblique strain. He's been ruled out for the Lakers' matchup against Portland on Tuesday but could have a chance to make his NBA debut Wednesday against the Clippers.

comment: The Lakers recalled Carr (oblique) from the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Tuesday, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
detail: Carr presumably joined the G League Lakers to get some practice reps in while working his way back from an oblique strain. His next chance to play for the parent club will come Wednesday against the Clippers in the second leg of the Lakers' back-to-back set.

comment: Demin posted 22 points (5-10 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 7-7 FT), four rebounds and six assists across 31 minutes in Saturday's 125-121 loss to the Cavaliers.
detail: Demin rebounded from a four-point season opener with a much stronger offensive performance, connecting on five triples after missing all five of his attempts Wednesday. His six assists were also encouraging after recording just two in his debut. The 31-minute workload suggests Brooklyn will continue giving him significant opportunities, although his shooting consistency remains a concern for fantasy managers. His long-term upside should be somewhere in the middle between this impressive outing and the struggles he endured in the opener.

comment: Ighodaro (oblique) is feeling better and considered day-to-day ahead of Friday's game against the Nuggets, John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports 98.7 FM reports.
detail: Ighodaro hasn't played since the regular-season opener due to an oblique strain, and he can be considered questionable for Friday until the Suns offer an update on his status. If the Marquette product remains sidelined against Denver, Khaman Maluach and Duop Reath would likely continue seeing increased playing time.

comment: Demin (undisclosed) exited Tuesday's game against the Celtics, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports.
detail: Demin hasn't had a good night, though it got even worse after he was seen limping off the floor back to the locker room with 2:22 left in the first half. If Demin can't return, it should mean more minutes for Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis.

comment: Demin (leg) won't return to Tuesday's game against Boston, C.J. Holmes of the New York Daily News reports. He finished with two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), one rebound, two assists and one steal over 10 minutes.
detail: Demin was seen holding his leg and eventually limped off the floor to the locker room with 2:22 left in the first half. The Nets don't play again until Friday versus Detroit, so he will have a few extra days to rest and recover. However, if Demin isn't available for that contest, Keon Ellis or Mikel Brown could replace him in the starting lineup. Either way, Ellis and Brown would be in line for more minutes.

comment: The Mavericks recalled Aldama (knee) from the G League's Texas Legends on Tuesday.
detail: Aldama presumably got some practice reps in with the Legends after being assigned to the squad earlier in the day. He's still working his way back from right knee surgery he underwent in March, and he's listed as doubtful for Wednesday's matchup with the Thunder.

comment: Demin (leg) stated he isn't sure if he will be able to play in Friday's game against Detroit, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Demin exited Tuesday's 125-124 overtime loss to the Celtics in the first half and didn't return. He isn't sure if he will play Friday versus the Pistons, though he indicated that the injury is "nothing serious," adding that he was kneed in the "muscle/bone area." The 20-year-old has had a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign, averaging 7.8 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.0 steals while shooting 28.6 percent from deep. If Demin isn't out there against Detroit, Nolan Traore, who also didn't return to Tuesday's meeting with the Celtics due to cramps, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for more minutes, with two of those players in line to start.

comment: The Warriors are exploring potential trades involving Porzingis (personal), who remains away from the team indefinitely while dealing with ongoing health concerns, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Porzingis is reportedly contemplating his future in basketball as he continues to battle health issues that have plagued him for nearly two years. Golden State isn't expecting the veteran center to rejoin the team anytime soon, and his contract structure could make him an attractive trade piece despite the uncertainty surrounding his playing future. With no timetable for his return and retirement potentially on the table, Porzingis remains a highly speculative fantasy stash, even in leagues with injured reserve spots.

comment: Wiggins (knee) is probable for Wednesday against Miami.
detail: Wiggins was previously considered questionable for Atlanta. However, he's trending in the right direction and appears ready to reprise his usual role.

comment: Joe (hip) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hornets.
detail: Joe will end up missing both legs of this back-to-back set. In his absence, the Pistons will likely lean on Ronald Holland, Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

comment: Thompson (ankle) is probable for Wednesday against the Hornets.
detail: Thompson returned from a one-game absence to post 11 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-3 FT), six rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block across 25 minutes in Tuesday's 111-97 loss to the Knicks. He appears to have walked away without any setbacks and is expected to play the second leg of this back-to-back set.

comment: Lendeborg (foot) went through Wednesday's morning shootaround, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
detail: The standout rookie remains officially listed as questionable for Wednesday's tilt versus Minnesota. However, he appears to be trending in the right direction.

comment: Smart (forearm) is out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks.
detail: Although he remains day-to-day, Smart will be sidelined for a third straight contest. Look for Reed Sheppard and Tari Eason to continue seeing hefty roles off the Houston bench in the meantime.

comment: Haliburton (hamstring) will miss time, though his timetable has yet to be announced, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Haliburton's official diagnosis is a left hamstring strain. Team doctors will continue to evaluate him, so fantasy managers will have to patiently wait for more clarity. In the meantime, the Pacers will need to lean more on Andrew Nembhard (neck), Quenton Jackson and Kelly Oubre.

comment: Carr (oblique) was assigned Wednesday to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports
detail: With the Lakers unlikely to hold much practice time over their current back-to-back set, this assignment gives Carr a chance to continue his recovery work with an oblique injury. The rookie guard was recalled Tuesday and could be brought back to the parent club at some point soon.

comment: Fontecchio (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against the Hawks.
detail: The veteran sharpshooter was previously listed as doubtful. His next chance to play comes Friday against the Pacers.

comment: Caruso (ankle) is expected to miss time due to an ankle sprain, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
detail: With Caruso already ruled out for Wednesday's game in Dallas due to an ankle sprain, it sounds like the veteran forward could remain sidelined beyond a one-game absence. That would leave Oklahoma City without one of its key rotation wings for at least the near term, which could force Jared McCain into a big role for the banged-up Thunder.

comment: Black (personal) was not present at Wednesday's morning shootaround, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
detail: Black is listed as questionable on the injury report. However, Beede reports that Black is expected back in time before tipoff, so fantasy managers can keep him in lineups for the time being.

comment: Marshall (illness) is now doubtful for Wednesday against the Thunder.
detail: Marshall was originally questionable, so he's trending in the wrong direction. With the Mavericks expected to hold him out, the team could rely more on Zaccharie Risacher.

comment: Biberovic (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Biberovic is still waiting to make his NBA debut. His next chance to do so arrives Friday against the Rockets.

comment: Aldama (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Aldama is still waiting to make his Mavericks debut. His next chance to return from knee surgery comes Friday versus Houston.

comment: Carr (oblique) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
detail: The rookie first-rounder will need more time to recover from the oblique injury that's kept him sidelined for what will be his fifth consecutive contest. Carr's next chance to suit up will come against the Warriors on Friday in the first Emirates NBA Cup matchup.

comment: Thiero (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
detail: Thiero will miss his fifth consecutive outing to begin the 2026-27 campaign with swelling in his left knee. His next chance to suit up will come against the Warriors on Friday in the first Emirates NBA Cup matchup.

comment: Williams (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
detail: Williams is sitting out the second part of this back-to-back set. Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jake LaRavia seem to be the most likely options to replace Williams in the starting lineup.

comment: Doncic (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
detail: Doncic is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set. Quentin Grimes appears to be the most likely candidate to replace Doncic in the starting lineup.

comment: Alvarado (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Bulls.
detail: Alvarado will miss a third straight game for New York. With the veteran guard out, Tyler Kolek will likely continue to pick up some backup point guard minutes.

comment: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Utah, Paul Garcia of ProjectSpurs.com reports.
detail: This will be Harris' fifth straight game on the shelf as the Spurs continue to wait for his official debut. Harris is progressing and is said to be close to day-to-day.

comment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

comment: Awaka (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
detail: Awaka will hit the sidelines after tweaking his ankle during Monday's 134-99 loss to the Celtics. For now, he should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting in Boston.

comment: Williams (adductor) won't play in Wednesday's game against the Knicks, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
detail: Williams continues to battle left adductor soreness. His next opportunity to make his season debut arrives Friday, when the Bulls square off with the Celtics in Boston.

comment: Marshall (illness) won't play in Wednesday's game against Oklahoma City.
detail: Marshall will now miss his second consecutive contest, meaning his next opportunity to suit up will come Friday against the Rockets. Without Marshall on the floor, Max Christie, Walter Clayton and Morez Johnson should each see a few extra minutes versus the Thunder.

comment: Johnson (ankle) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
detail: Johnson will miss his third consecutive game, so his next opportunity to suit up will come Friday in Phoenix. Without Johnson on the floor, Bryce Hopkins is expected to remain in the starting lineup.

comment: Santos has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves due to left knee tendinitis.
detail: Santos was a late addition to the injury report before being ruled out shortly thereafter. With the 24-year-old forward sidelined, Georges Niang will likely see a bump in minutes. Santos' next opportunity to play will come Friday against the Lakers.

comment: Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle stated McConnell (hamstring) is "doing better" and "getting closer" to a return, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
detail: McConnell hasn't played this season due to a hamstring injury. While Carlisle didn't give a specific date on when McConnell will be cleared to suit up, it appears his return will come sooner rather than later. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) sidelined, McConnell could work his way into the starting lineup at some point, though it may take him at least a few games before he receives a full workload.

comment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

comment: Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least the next two weeks of action, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries, the Pacers will likely take their time bringing Haliburton back to the court, so don't be surprised if his absence extends beyond this two-week window. Andrew Nembhard (neck) and Pascal Siakam should each get a usage bump as they take over more of the playmaking duties sans Haliburton and there will be more minutes available for Quenton Jackson.

comment: Strus (foot) is making progress but is set to miss at least one more week, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Strus sustained a partially torn plantar fascia in his right foot in the Clippers' preseason opener but is seemingly nearing a return to game action. Keaton Wagler and Kobe Sanders will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Strus and Brandon Ingram (Achilles) are sidelined.

comment: Ingram (Achilles) is making progress but is set to miss at least one more week, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Ingram has yet to make his season debut while recovering from a partially torn Achilles, though he's seemingly getting closer to a return to action. In the meantime, Gradey Dick and Kobe Sanders will likely continue seeing increased burn.

comment: Shamet (ankle) exited Wednesday's game against the Bulls, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: After a dunk in the second quarter, Shamet inadvertently stepped on Caleb Wilson's foot. He immediately grabbed his right ankle/foot and exited the contest. Shamet has since made his way to the bench, though until he's back on the floor, he should be considered questionable to return.

comment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

comment: Markkanen (wrist) is out for Wednesday's tilt against the Spurs.
detail: After being listed as questionable to suit up due to a right wrist sprain suffered in Utah's 110-105 loss to Memphis on Monday, Markkanen has been downgraded to out. With Jusuf Nurkic (toe) and Jaren Jackson (knee) both sidelined, Jaxson Hayes, Brice Sensabaugh, Kyle Filipowski and Svi Mykhailiuk are all candidates to earn more playing time.

comment: Johnson has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers due to right Achilles soreness.
detail: The Achilles soreness is a new issue for Johnson, who was a late scratch ahead of tipoff. His next chance to play will come Friday against the Hornets. With the 2025 No. 6 overall pick sidelined, Bilal Coulibaly and Bub Carrington could see increased playing time.

comment: Niederhauser (foot) remains out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers. He also won't travel with the team for the upcoming two-game road trip in Minnesota and Golden State, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Niederhauser hasn't played this season and is working his way back from surgery in March. He's "making progress," though it's unknown when he will be back on the floor. The 2025 No. 30 overall pick appeared in 41 regular-season games as a rookie, averaging 4.3 points and 2.9 rebounds. Niederhauser will presumably be eased back into action once he's cleared to suit up, but until that happens, Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez should handle most of the work in the middle.

comment: Poole (ankle) won't return to Wednesday's game against the Nuggets. He finished with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt), one rebound and one steal over seven minutes.
detail: Poole was on the injury report heading into the contest due to an illness. While he was able to suit up, he has been ruled out due to an ankle injury suffered in the first half. The Pelicans play again Thursday versus the Kings, so Poole should at least be considered questionable for that contest.

comment: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
detail: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

comment: Knueppel (hamstring) will practice with the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Thursday, the Hornets announced.
detail: Although the second-year sharpshooter hasn't been given an official timetable, this suggests that he's progressing towards a return. Knueppel will almost certainly be recalled shortly after practice, though an update on his progress may not be given immediately.

comment: Thomas (foot) is questionable for Thursday's game in Atlanta.
detail: Thomas is at risk of sitting out the second end of this back-to-back set. Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja could get on the streaming radar Thursday, especially if Jaylon Tyson (neck) is sidelined.

comment: Tyson (neck) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Hawks.
detail: Tyson was a late addition to the injury report due to a cervical strain. He's played a modest role with the second unit to open the season, averaging 9.0 points, 3.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 0.8 steals in 21.5 minutes per game.

comment: Poole (ankle) is now doubtful for Thursday against the Kings.
detail: Poole appears likely to miss the second leg of this back-to-back set. The veteran left Wednesday's game against Denver after just seven minutes and failed to return. His absence could open things up a bit for Bennedict Mathurin.

comment: Leonard (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least three to four weeks, Chris Haynes of NBA TV reports.
detail: The extended absence represents a significant setback for Leonard, who will be unavailable for the foreseeable future. His absence should create additional offensive opportunities for Toronto's remaining rotation players, with guys like RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Allen Graves seeing more usage. Leonard's recovery timeline will be worth monitoring, as the reported window represents a minimum absence rather than a firm return date.

comment: Williams (adductor) is questionable for Friday's game in Boston.
detail: Williams is looking to be available for his season debut Friday. The forward could test out the issue prior to Friday's contest before Chicago clarifies his status.

comment: Smith is questionable for Friday's game against Boston with a left finger sprain.
detail: This is a new injury for Chicago's starting center, but he's considered day-to-day. If Smith is held out against Boston, the Bulls could lean more on Zach Collins.

comment: Awaka (ankle) is questionable for Friday's game in Boston.
detail: Awaka continues to battle a left ankle sprain. The rookie big man could go through morning shootaround and pregame warmups before the Bulls update his status.

comment: Joe (hip) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Brooklyn.
detail: Joe has missed Detroit's last two games due to a right hip contusion, but his questionable designation suggests he could return Friday. The 27-year-old guard has appeared in three games this season, averaging 7.3 points in 13.9 minutes per contest. If Joe remains sidelined, Kevin Huerter, Ronald Holland and Javonte Green could continue seeing additional opportunities off the bench.

comment: Sheppard (back) is out for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
detail: The combo guard is sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set. With Sheppard getting Friday night off, Tari Eason should be able to maintain a prominent role off the bench even if Alperen Sengun (back) returns to action.

comment: Smart (forearm) is questionable for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
detail: Smart has missed three consecutive games due to a left forearm strain, but he could return to action Friday. The veteran guard last played Oct. 23 against San Antonio, and his potential return would provide Houston with additional backcourt depth. If Smart remains sidelined, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton could continue seeing increased opportunities.

comment: Sengun (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Mavericks.
detail: Sengun has a chance to return from a one-game absence with a back issue. If the star big man indeed gets back in the lineup, less playing time will be available at center for Tari Eason and Clint Capela.

comment: Nembhard (neck) is listed as probable for Friday's game against Miami.
detail: Nembhard has been battling some lingering neck stiffness, though he's likely to play Friday. He's coming off an 18-point, 14-assist double-double in Wednesday's loss to Philadelphia and should continue taking on increased playmaking responsibilities in Tyrese Haliburton's (hamstring) stead.

comment: Nesmith (hamstring) is probable for Friday's game against the Heat.

detail: This will be Watson's second straight game on the sidelines, and with Friday's game being the first of a back-to-back set, he may need to spend an additional game on the inactive list. Meleek Thomas, Sam Merrill and Mario Hezonja will help pick up the slack in Watson's absence.

comment: Christie (hip) is out for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: The swingman is missing his first game of the season with a hip injury , which he suffered Monday against the Kings. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher stand out as the most likely candidates to step into the starting lineup Wednesday.

comment: Aldama (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
detail: The questionable tag is an upgrade for Aldama, who has either been listed as out or doubtful ahead of all of Dallas' games this season. If the 25-year-old is cleared to make his season debut following knee surgery, he'll likely operate under a minutes restriction.

detail: Johnson has already missed three games. However, it doesn't appear he will be sidelined Wednesday versus the Raptors. comment: Diallo (wrist) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.

detail: Capela is in danger of missing his second consecutive contest and third overall of the 2026-27 campaign. With Steven Adams (calf) sidelined, Jabari Smith may spend more time in the middle behind Alperen Sengun. Oscar Tshiebwe might also see a few minutes off the bench.

comment: Zubac (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
detail: Zubac has missed the last five regular-season games due to an ankle injury. If Zubac is sidelined again Wednesday versus Memphis, Jay Huff is expected to remain in the starting lineup at the five.

comment: Oubre (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
detail: Oubre is trying to move past a knee contusion Wednesday. Less playing time would be available for Jarace Walker if Oubre is healthy enough to play.

comment: Toppin (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.

comment: Post (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Indiana.
detail: Post is in danger of missing his third consecutive contest because of a right ankle sprain. If Post remains sidelined Wednesday versus the Pacers, Kris Murray should continue to see more minutes.

comment: Pippen (back) won't play Wednesday against the Pacers.
detail: This will be Pippen's third straight game on the sidelines, which should continue resulting in more minutes for Cam Spencer. Pippen's next chance to play will come Friday against the Thunder.

comment: Gardner (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.

comment: Antetokounmpo is probable to play Wednesday against the Clippers due to a sprained right wrist.
detail: Antetokounmpo is dealing with a sprained wrist on his shooting hand, but it doesn't appear he has any intention of sitting out Wednesday's game. Check back closer to Wednesday's tipoff for official confirmation on his status.

comment: Shannon (hip) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game in Houston.
detail: Shannon didn't play in Monday's 112-100 win over Milwaukee. If Shannon misses his second consecutive game, Cody Williams, Trey Lyles and Jaylen Clark could each see more minutes.

comment: Poole (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Utah.
detail: Poole is expected to return from a three-game layoff for the meeting with the Jazz on Wednesday. The 27-year-old hasn't had a memorable 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 6.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals across 16.0 minutes per contest. If Poole is cleared for action, it would likely mean fewer minutes for Bryce McGowens and Trendon Watford.

comment: Murphy (knee) is probable for Wednesday's game versus the Jazz.
detail: Murphy played through the knee issues and logged 40 minutes in Monday's 135-134 win over the Grizzlies, so it clearly didn't impact his playing time. It appears he'll continue to push through the pain Wednesday.

comment: Topic (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
detail: Topic has yet to play during the 2026-27 campaign, and at this rate, it doesn't look like he will be on the floor anytime soon. For now, he should be considered week-to-week. comment: Sorber (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.

comment: Fleming is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Trail Blazers due to a sprained left ankle, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
detail: Fleming must have tweaked his ankle at practice because he's been out of the rotation the past two games. The Suns will update his status closer to Wednesday's tip.

comment: Achiuwa (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
detail: Achiuwa is currently bothered by left ankle soreness, though it doesn't appear as if it will be enough to keep him off the floor against Los Angeles. The 27-year-old has played well in his seven regular-season appearances in 2026-27, averaging 11.6 points and 1.9 steals, both career highs, along with 6.6 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.0 blocks over 28.6 minutes per contest.

comment: Leonard has completed treatment to reduce swelling in his left knee and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Leonard will now begin the next phase of his rehab, and while he'll be re-evaluated by Nov. 10, it's still unlikely we'll see him back on the floor until the end of November. Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to start while Leonard is sidelined, and it'll be Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett running the show on offense.

comment: Poeltl is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets due to left shoulder bursitis, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
detail: Poeltl is looking to avoid a third straight absence with the issue. If the veteran big man is unable to give it a go Wednesday, Collin Murray-Boyles should take on the lion's share of the center minutes for the Raptors.

comment: Nurkic (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans.
detail: Nurkic has been a spectator to begin the season, and he's still not ready for game action due to a foot injury. The veteran big man should be considered week-to-week until the Jazz update his recovery, so Jaxson Hayes should remain the team's primary center going forward.

comment: Bamba is questionable for Wednesday's game in New Orleans due to a sprained right ankle.
detail: Bamba must have tweaked his ankle during Monday's 119-97 loss to the Spurs, and now he's in danger of sitting out Wednesday's game. If Bamba is forced to the sidelines, Kyle Filipowski would likely pick up most of his minutes.

comment: Gill (back) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
detail: Gill's availability is uncertain as Washington deals with multiple injuries in its frontcourt. Gill's status should become clearer closer to tipoff, though he remains a limited fantasy option even if cleared to play.

comment: Sarr (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
detail: Sarr is dealing with left knee soreness that could force him to miss another contest after sitting out Monday's win over Orlando. comment: Aldama (knee) is doubtful for Wednesday's game against the Spurs, per NBA reporter Marc Stein.
detail: Despite going through shootaround, Aldama still doesn't appear to be ready for his season debut. Assuming he's later ruled out, Aldama's next chance to play would come Friday against Utah.

Golden State continues to explore trading the 31-year-old center's contract ahead of the Feb. 11 deadline rather than voiding his deal. With Porzingis reportedly leaning toward retirement and no timetable for his return, he remains an extremely risky fantasy investment with little reason to expect meaningful production this season.

comment: Capela (ankle) is out for Wednesday's game against the Timberwolves.

comment: Jones (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday against the Celtics.

comment: Carter (illness) practiced with the G League's Maine Celtics on Wednesday.
detail: Carter is working back from mononucleosis, which has prevented him from making his season debut. A two-way player, Carter figures to begin his season in Maine as opposed to Boston once healthy.

comment: Sharpe registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 win over the Pacers.

It was also the second time he scored in double digits this season. Sharpe's rebounding provides a useful foundation, although his ceiling will depend on whether Brooklyn consistently gives him enough touches and playing time -- he has played more than 25 minutes just twice all season long.

comment: Clowney won't return to Wednesday's game against the Hornets due to right knee soreness. He'll finish with seven points (3-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one assist across 17 minutes.
detail: Chaney Johnson and Josh Minott are candidates to pick up a few extra minutes in Clowney's stead. His next chance to suit up will come Saturday at Atlanta.

comment: Reaves (heel) won't undergo imaging and is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Suns, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
detail: An official designation for Reaves' status will be given Saturday, according to Buha, and head coach JJ Redick also said Reaves has a bruise on his heel. The star guard is enjoying an excellent start to the season and is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game. If he's sidelined, expect Ziaire Williams to start in the backcourt alongside Luka Doncic.

comment: Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Doncic (ankle) is "fine," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
detail: The superstar guard exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's win over the Bucks due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return. Doncic can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable marker until the Lakers release an official injury report at some point prior to Sunday's matchup in Phoenix.

comment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

comment: Achiuwa (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
detail: Achiuwa is sitting out Friday for the first time this season due to left ankle soreness, and he can be deemed day-to-day going forward. His absence likely paves the way for Keegan Murray to re-enter the starting lineup after opening 2026-27 as the Kings' starting power forward.
